_comment:
Derived by measuring 400 APIGen-MT retail conversations, and the result is mostly negative, which is the point of writing it down.

The premise of this library is that a domain has a high-frequency mutable entity that is genuinely last-write-wins. Measured on retail customer service, that is close to false:

  entity            spoken   machine   machine share   supersedes
  delivery_address     51      1048            95%          15%  (26 of 400 convs)
  payment_method      141      3701            86%           1%  (109 convs)
  order_id            625      2340            79%           5%  (309 convs)
  refund_amount      2280         -             -           93%  (388 convs)

Three findings, and the first two are negative:

1. 79-95% of every entity's mentions live in tool output, which the read path may
   not read. This is the same structural limit found in the airline domain, and it
   is a property of tool-heavy support traffic rather than of this tracker.

2. Supersession is rare. Payment method changes in 1% of conversations, the order
   in 5%. A last-write-wins tracker has almost nothing to overwrite here. This is
   the honest headline: retail is a poor fit, and no amount of pattern tuning
   changes that.

3. refund_amount is deliberately absent despite being the most-mentioned quantity
   in the data, at 2,280 spoken mentions. It 'changes' in 93% of conversations
   because a retail conversation contains many different dollar amounts -- item
   prices, totals, price differences -- not because one of them is being
   corrected. Putting them in one last-write-wins slot would be the same mistake
   as modelling origin and destination as a single airport code, and the same
   mistake as the schema this file replaces. A slot that changes constantly
   because it means several things at once tracks nothing.

So this schema tracks the two entities that survive the measurement. delivery_address
is the one genuine last-write-wins slot: a delivery has one address and the user can
change it, which is what modify_pending_order_address exists for. It is required to
look like a street address, because that is the only shape that distinguishes an
address from the payment methods and prose that broke the previous version.

payment_method is included because it is spoken (141 mentions) and is a real piece
of current state even though it rarely changes. It is matched only with a
possessive or a payment verb, so 'use my gift card' records a payment method
rather than a destination.

payment_method: \b(?:my|the|our)\s+(?:existing\s+|saved\s+|current\s+)?(gift card|gift card balance|credit card|paypal|paypal account|debit card)\b
